title: Nuclear supply chain atrophy
bottleneck: Three decades of minimal new build have hollowed out the Western nuclear supply chain: heavy forging capacity for reactor vessels, specialized valve and pump manufacturers, and nuclear-grade instrumentation suppliers have shrunk or vanished. Rebuilding fabrication capacity requires multi-year capital investment that suppliers will only make against firm orders, which developers will only place once suppliers exist. First projects pay the full cost of supply-chain resurrection. Without domestic forging capacity, projects depend on a small number of foreign suppliers, adding geopolitical risk to already fragile schedules.
why_it_blocks: This chicken-and-egg dilemma inflates first-of-a-kind costs and stretches schedules, killing projects before they demonstrate the economics that would justify the supply chain.
current_state: A few large forgings have been ordered for current projects. Broad commercial-scale fabrication capacity will only emerge after sustained order books materialize.
